notes: 18 key claims plus 6 other dossier items. Confirmed key claims: 1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,15,16,17,18. Corrected key claims: 5 (the machine isn't named for the Oct 13-14 runs; the film's own run is a single-session record) and 14 (the drop from 21,229 to 4,251 took two steps). Also corrected: the GPU-cases overstatement, the README line citations, the emitFrontmost direction, the pinned commit's description. Unverifiable: quote 11 (the X post), kept UNVERIFIED. Executing repo code was denied, so 'about 9 s' for the tests and the 40.9-44.2 µs film run were not reproduced. 127 tests confirmed statically.

corrections.original: Claim 5: '25.1-25.3 µs at 4,251-4,254 ops (Oct 13-14, author's M5 Max)'; misconception 7 'The author's runs used an Apple M5 Max'.
corrections.fix: status.md doesn't name the machine for the Oct 13-14 runs (25.1-25.3 µs on Oct 13 at load 3.7-4.2; 25.2-25.3 µs on Oct 14), nor for the 35.76 µs median (load 1.5-1.7). M5 Max is stated only for the Sept 16/17 runs and some doc measurements. Caption without a machine. The film's 40.92/42.13/44.20 µs (M4 Max, load ~10.5) is a single-session record that no one reproduced.

corrections.original: Claim 14 / hook 8: the program went from 21,229 to 4,251 ops 'by handing text back to the browser's own textarea'; §7 'about 4.6× smaller'.
corrections.fix: Two steps on Oct 13: merging Files into Monitor took 21,229 ops / 230 layers to 19,851 / 217. That evening the textarea took 19,851 to 4,251 ops / 123 layers (about 4.7× smaller; 113.8-114.8 µs to 25.1-25.3 µs, about 4.5× faster).

corrections.original: §4: 'The GPU wins only when one program runs over many tables that stay on the GPU, as in JSON search.'
corrections.fix: patterns.md names two cases: a tree of matrix products run one dispatch per level (knuth-plass, 0.47 ms on WebGPU against 3.4 ms on the CPU), and one program over many tables that stay on the GPU (JSON search).

corrections.original: README citations: S1 L8 (tests), L23 (viewport), L30 (Photos zoom), L32 (Monitor), L33 (Notes, quote 9), L45-L57 (files).
corrections.fix: At 257856e: tests L9, viewport L22, Photos L29, Monitor L30, Notes L31, files table L35-L44.

corrections.original: §5d: 'emitFrontmost walks stacking ranks front to back'; the hit test is '13 operations in 4 layers per rectangle'.
corrections.fix: The code checks ranks one at a time, looping from rank windowCount-1 down to 0, and no source says which end is the front. The hit test is '13 operations in 4 layers per rectangle once the edges exist', with edge bits shared between rectangles, comparing distance >= 0.5.

corrections.original: Pinned commit 257856e described as 'a lab commit'.
corrections.fix: 257856e is a merge commit (parents 4ea7fcb, e86c1b4) bringing in the recovery-parser lab experiment; author date 2026-10-16; no HandwiredOS change.

corrections.original: Sept 16 WebGPU row and focused-window description lacked conditions / cited CSS for the filled title dot.
corrections.fix: Added Bun 1.4.0 and load average 4-6, and noted that the 4-window, 14,019-op program was measured before the Sept 17 pass and that the drag was Files over Notes. The filled title dot is now cited to the screenshot; the CSS gives the 7% copper wash and the 24% hairline.

corrections.original: Quote 11: "Isn't a neural net probabilistic? Yes if you train it, no if you hand-wrote the weights that correspond exactly to your program" (Cheng Lou on X).
corrections.fix: Keep it UNVERIFIED and do not use it as a quote. Only a members-only Medium article carries it, and its excerpt ends ', lol 🙂'. The original X post was not found on 2026-10-27.
